venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner ran it until they sat. White made him hold it. Here is how Saturday actually looked.
headline: Florida did not trick FAU. They stretched the field, handed it to Baugh, and threw it now when the defense sat down. White rushed four, took the deep ball away, and waited. When that wait paid, Coleman and Johnson were standing in the window. When a job was lost, FAU scored.

offense.body:
Florida opened Saturday the same way they intended to play the rest of it. First-and-10 from their own 6, 12:00 left in the first, Philo in the shotgun, Baugh next to him, one tight end, three receivers. That is 11 personnel — three wide so FAU cannot load the box and still cover Brown, Wilson, and Stockton. They huddle. They line up. They give it to Baugh. Nine yards. Faulkner’s first answer is not a shot play. It is the best player, downhill, after they have already spread you out.

Two minutes later they are at their own 23 and the picture has not changed. Corners sitting off. Philo does not hunt it. Hitch to Brown, eight yards, on time. After they drop him on the next series, he comes right back: Wilson, short left, 19 yards, first down. Stay on the field. Come back to the run. That is the rhythm of this offense. It is not a trick show. It is a count.

The snap that explains the night is first-and-10 at the FAU 49 with 8:49 left in the first. Same 11. Baugh on Philo’s left. Three receivers to the field, one to the boundary. The tight end is split out in the trips — he is not jammed on the tackle. FAU is in two-high and the corners are eight yards off. Faulkner is reading the numbers. If they bring a body down into the box, Baugh has the give. They do not. They sit. So Philo throws the hitch to Brown. Catch at the 50. First man misses. Brown runs 49 yards and the Swamp has its first touchdown of the Sumrall era.

People will remember the score. The play is the throw. Five yards, on time, after they refused the run. Brown is in that window because he makes the first miss. Everything else Saturday is that idea showing up in a different jersey.

When the front clogs, Baugh does not wait on it. At 7:17 he takes it left, the hole dies, he plants and bounces 18. Same family as the first snap. If the end crashes, he is already outside. From the 12 they throw it now to Stockton on the right and he finishes. Then they hand Brown the run they have been throwing him — 14 yards to the left on second-and-4. Manufactured. Not a gadget they hid.

FAU finally scores, and the safety starts cheating Baugh because he has been eating. Second quarter, 13:22, second-and-6 from the Florida 29. Extra bodies stay in to protect. Abrams runs by everybody down the right sideline. Sixty-three yards to the 8. That shot only exists because the run was real. Faulkner does not open the night hunting it. He takes the lid off when they come down.

Fourth-and-3 from the 3, 11:05 of the second. He empties the backfield. Five out. The ends have to declare, and they climb the pocket. Contain is gone. Philo walks in. If they stay home, he has five to throw to. The keep is live because of how he lined them up.

Baugh scores from 12 on a backside cut and from 7 with the pad down. Then, third-and-2 at the Florida 33, 13:59 of the third, the crease opens and he is gone 61 yards to the 6. They run it through the pile on the next snap. Faulkner said in the spring he would run it when the whole stadium knew. That series is him keeping the promise.

They sit for Baugh again in the third and Philo goes over the top to Brown for 33. Later Clark is the back, the linebackers sit for the run, he releases, catch at the 4, he drives it in. The back becomes the receiver because they finally stopped the run with their eyes.

The other side of hitch is what happens when he holds it. Third-and-7 at the FAU 44, 44 seconds left in the half. The window is there and then it is not. Sweeney sits and takes it. The rhythm throw is this offense. When Philo waits, the play dies.

What Saturday was: 11, shotgun, Baugh until they sit, hitch, then the go. Empty when he wants the ends to climb. Campbell will see the same picture. The question is whether they sit.
bullets: They stretch the field, run Baugh, and throw it now when the corners sit.
Brown’s 49 is a hitch and a miss — not a bomb.
Abrams’ 63 and the empty keep only exist because the run was real.
When Philo holds it, Sweeney is sitting.

defense.body:
White’s answer to a spread team that does not huddle is simple enough for fans and hard enough to play. Four down. Two linebackers. An extra defensive back on the slot. Corners off so nothing goes over their head. Rush four. Tackle the five-yard throw. Do not get cute.

The tax shows up on the first third down. FAU, shotgun, one back, 14:27 of the first, third-and-7 from their own 28. Corners are off. Veltkamp throws hitch to Henry. Ten yards. Converted. White will live with that throw if they tackle. That is the deal opening the night: give them the short one, kill the explosive.

The deal pays at 12:07. Third-and-10 at the Florida 35. Veltkamp in the gun, trips one side. White does not send the house. Four rush. Two safeties high. Everybody else drops. The ball comes out late. Coleman is already in the lane. He catches it at the 5 and the drive is over. That is the defense working. Make him hold it. Do not open a window with a blitz.

The rest of the night is that plan, and the jobs inside it.

First-and-goal at the 1, 13:55 of the second. White packs the box. No bounce. You have to win this yard. Ervin still walks in. The front was right. They lost the pile. Phone booth. That is a job, not a surprise call.

Third-and-7 at the 7, 6:52 of the second. Same four-rush as Coleman’s pick. Veltkamp feels it, leaves, dives the pylon. Watch the end. His job is stay outside and keep the quarterback in. He does not. Same call. Different job lost. Contain.

Then the wait pays again. First snap after Baugh scores, 4:01 of the second, FAU at their own 25. Heat up the middle. Veltkamp throws off his back foot. Johnson goes up and gets it at the 30. Coleman is on the breakup. Same idea as 12:07. He held it. They took it.

Late in the third they fade you. First-and-10 at the Florida 20. Corners have been sitting off all night — that is the point of the defense. Valsin releases outside, stacks Flowers, wins the back line. Twenty-yard score. If you sit off to kill the deep ball, you have to win the fade when they throw it. Same play Stockton ran the other way.

In the fourth, fourth-and-1 at the 1, Veltkamp keeps left. Bett gets there. Ball out at the 5. Myles Johnson falls on it at the 11. The rush finally finishes. White has been waiting all night. This time the guy wins his one-on-one.

What Saturday was: four down, extra DB on the slot, rush four, no deep ball. Coleman and Johnson are that plan. The sloppy part is the hitch they agreed to live with, plus the pile, the edge, and the fade. Campbell will throw the short one and run the quarterback. Same two jobs. Slot and the end who cannot leave.
bullets: Four rush, two-high. Make him hold it. Coleman and Johnson are that plan.
The hitch convert is the tax. White will live with it if they tackle.
They lose when the pile loses, the end leaves, or the fade wins the back line.
Campbell: short throw and the quarterback run.

specials.body: Fourth-and-4 from the FAU 35, 2:10 left in the first. They can go for it. They let Durkin try it from 53 instead. Clean. 17–0, and Florida never punts. They took the points when the drive stalled and they never gave the ball back on fourth down the rest of the night.
bullets: Durkin from 53. They took the points.

keys: Faulkner stretches them, runs Baugh, and throws it now when they sit. Brown’s 49 is that throw.
When they cheat the run, he takes the lid off. Abrams. Empty at the 3. The keep is live because of how he lined them up.
White rushes four and waits. Coleman and Johnson are the wait paying off.
They lose when the pile, the edge, or the fade loses. Campbell will throw hitch and run the quarterback.

nextWeek.look: They will go fast and throw hitch. Faulkner will still run Baugh until they sit. White will still rush four. The snaps that matter are the short throw and whether the end stays home.
